title: _safePay revert in stake()/unstake() can trap users who want to adjust their principal during a temporary reward shortfall
description:
`_safePay` now reverts if `rewardToken.balanceOf(address(this)) < amount` (line 302). The fix correctly addresses the prior CS-01 silent-forfeiture bug for `claim()`. However, the same `_safePay` is invoked inside `stake()` (line 253) and `unstake()` (line 271) as part of the auto-claim that runs when `user.amount > 0`.

Consequence: if pending rewards exceed the on-contract balance (e.g., the dispatcher is lagging on mint-debt realisation, the dispatcher hook is unset/broken, or another user just drained the balance in the same block), a user who merely wants to stake MORE or unstake SOME of their principal cannot do so — the entire transaction reverts on the auto-claim. The only remaining escape is `emergencyWithdraw`, which forfeits the user's entire pending reward (not just the unpayable portion).

This is strictly a user-experience regression: pre-fix, a user could stake/unstake and silently lose the unpayable portion of their reward (CS-01); post-fix, the user cannot adjust principal at all without forfeiting their ENTIRE accrued reward via the emergency path. For a short, transient shortfall the user can just wait and retry — acceptable. For a persistent shortfall (broken hook, owner mis-parameterisation), the user is trapped between 'cannot stake/unstake' and 'emergency-withdraw forfeits everything'.
impact: Principal adjustments (stake more, unstake partial) are blocked during any shortfall window, even when the user would gladly receive a partial payout and would NOT otherwise trigger a claim. The emergency-withdraw fallback is all-or-nothing (full exit of principal AND full forfeiture of pending reward), which is disproportionate when the shortfall is small relative to pending. Users who wanted to adjust, not exit, have no proportional option.
proof:
1. User has `user.amount = 100` and has accrued `pending = 50 phUSD`.
2. Dispatcher hook is temporarily unavailable; contract balance drops to `30 phUSD` because another user just claimed.
3. User calls `stake(10)` — intending to increase their position. `_syncBudget()` runs (balance unchanged because hook is unavailable), then `pending = 50`, `_safePay(50)` reverts because `30 < 50`. Entire tx reverts. User cannot stake.
4. User calls `unstake(50)` — intending to partially exit. Same revert path. User cannot unstake.
5. User's only option is `emergencyWithdraw`, which returns all 100 NFT units but forfeits the full 50 phUSD pending reward. If the shortfall is transient (hook catches up in minutes) the user would have been better off waiting — but they have no way to know.
suggested-fix:
Preferred: decouple principal-adjustment from reward-payout by making the auto-claim inside `stake/unstake` conditional on the ability to pay. Specifically, inside `stake` and `unstake`, catch the balance-short case and ROLL OVER the unpaid portion rather than reverting — i.e. set `user.rewardDebt = (user.amount * accRewardPerShare) / ACC_PRECISION - unpaid` so the unpaid amount remains claimable next time, then proceed with the principal change. This preserves the CS-01 fix (no silent forfeiture — the amount stays owed) while decoupling principal adjustments from transient reward-balance state.

Alternative: expose a separate `stakeNoClaim` / `unstakeNoClaim` path, or have `stake(amount)` accept a `skipClaim` flag. Less clean but avoids changing the core payout logic.

Alternative (minimal): keep the revert in `_safePay`, but in `stake`/`unstake`, treat the revert as a signal to skip the claim and proceed with the principal change (try/catch the transfer call). Messy but unblocks users.
